courses.title: Preparing for College and Careers
courses.description: Addresses the knowledge, skills, and behaviors all students need for success in college, career, and life, focusing on the impact of today's choices on tomorrow's possibilities. Topics include 21st-century life and career skills, exploration of personal aptitudes and goals, reviewing Indiana's College and Career Pathways, reviewing graduation plans, developing career plans, and building personal/career portfolios.

courses.title: Introduction to Housing and Interior Design
special_notes: CONFIRMED by owner: still offered for 2026-27, but will NOT be offered starting 2027-28 per state discontinuation. Site should stop showing this course for the 2027-28 catalog update.
courses.description: Addresses the selection and planning of designed spaces to meet the needs, wants, values, and lifestyles of individuals, families, clients, and communities, exploring housing decisions, resources, and options. Covers basic historical architectural styling, furniture styles, and elements/principles of design, along with space planning, floor plans, and construction documents. This course counts toward the Fine Arts credit requirement for the Core 40 with Academic Honors diploma.

courses.title: Introduction to Public Service
special_notes: IDOE names this as the preferred course to satisfy the Enlistment & Service Honors Seal public service requirement (per diploma FAQ).
courses.description: Introduces students to the many ways people serve their communities and country through military and civilian roles, exploring U.S. public service history, military traditions, ethical decision-making, leadership, and teamwork. Students examine career opportunities in government, public safety, and the military while gaining knowledge and skills to consider their own path in public service.

courses.title: Principles of Culinary Arts & Hospitality
courses.description: Focuses on the art of hospitality through food preparation skills and an understanding of the tourism and hospitality industry, developing understanding of career opportunities and responsibilities in food service and lodging. Introduces procedures for decision making affecting operation management, products, labor, and revenue, along with fundamentals of food preparation, sanitation, service procedures, and safety practices.

courses.title: Nutrition
courses.description: Students learn the characteristics, functions, and food sources of major nutrient groups and how to maximize nutrient retention in food preparation and storage, applying nutrient-needs knowledge throughout the life cycle to menu planning and food preparation. Engages students in hands-on learning of nutritional concepts, focused primarily on nutrition concepts with minimal cooking or hands-on food preparation.

courses.title: Culinary Arts
courses.description: Teaches students how to prepare the four major stocks, the five mother sauces (plus smaller sauces), and various soups, with emphasis on further development of classical cooking methods. Presents baking science fundamentals including terminology, ingredients, weights and measures, and proper equipment care, with students producing yeast goods, pies, cakes, cookies, and quick breads.

courses.title: Principles of Early Childhood Education
courses.description: Provides an overview of skills and strategies necessary to successfully complete a certificate, along with the history, theory, and foundations of early childhood education. Examines basic principles of child development, Developmentally Appropriate Practices, family importance, licensing, and quality care elements related to health, safety, and nutrition. For students interested in careers with young children such as education, psychology, pediatrics, nursing, or counseling. Studies physical, social, emotional, and intellectual development of children newborn to age eight, plus parenting, pregnancy, brain development, guidance and discipline, child abuse, children's literature, health/wellness, and early childhood careers.

courses.title: Early Childhood Education Curriculum
special_notes: Pre/co-requisite; Juniors/Seniors with C- or better may do classroom placements
courses.description: Examines developmentally appropriate environments and activities in various childcare settings while exploring developmental levels and cultural backgrounds of children ages birth to 8. Provides exposure to K-3 elementary education, developmental preschool, and community-based early childhood programs. Juniors/Seniors with C- or better may participate in an Elementary School or Early Childhood classroom during Block Days, planning and implementing lessons and completing an observation project.

courses.title: Early Childhood Education Guidance
courses.description: Allows students to analyze developmentally appropriate guidance, theory, and implementation for various early care and education settings, along with a basic understanding of anti-bias/multicultural emphasis in early childhood. Continues coverage of children from birth to age 8, requiring observations and field experiences as related to the course.

courses.title: Principles of Teaching Dual Credit
courses.description: Provides a general introduction to the field of teaching, exploring educational careers, teaching preparation, professional expectations, and requirements for teacher certification, along with current trends and issues in education.

courses.title: Child and Adolescent Development Dual Credit
courses.description: Examines the physical, social, emotional, cognitive, and moral development of the child from birth through adolescence, with a focus on the middle years through adolescence. Explores basic theories of child development, biological and environmental foundations, and the study of children through observation and interviewing techniques, along with the influence of parents, peers, school, culture, and media.

courses.title: Teaching and Learning Dual Credit
special_notes: May require ~20 hours of observation experience in local schools; students must follow a Code of Ethics to leave the building
courses.description: Provides the opportunity to apply concepts learned throughout the Education Professions pathway, focusing on best practices and introducing the role technology plays in the modern classroom. Through hands-on experience with educational software and hardware, students analyze ways to integrate technology as a tool for instruction, evaluation, and management, going out into township schools to serve as "student teachers." An observation experience of 20 hours may be required, and students must adhere to a Code of Ethics to leave the building.

courses.title: Principles of Fashion and Textiles
special_notes: CONFIRMED by owner: this is course 7301 per the CTD and NLPS documents - a DIFFERENT course than the discontinued 5380 'Introduction to Fashion & Textiles'. No conflict; correctly active.
courses.description: Prepares students for occupations and higher education programs related to the entire spectrum of fashion industry careers, building a foundation for all aspects of the fashion creation process. Major topics include basic clothing industry careers, construction techniques, pattern alterations, and use of commercial patterns.

courses.title: Textiles, Apparel & Merchandising
courses.description: Provides a comprehensive overview of the textiles, apparel, and merchandising industry specific to fashion-related goods, including the nature of fashion, raw materials and production, designers, retailers, and supporting services. Students demonstrate proficiency in construction, alteration, and mending of garments, and master merchandising of brands and products, with major topics including customer service and supply chain.

courses.title: Advanced Textiles
courses.description: Focuses on the study of textiles concerning fiber, yarn, fabric construction, and finishes affecting selection, use, and care. Students expand knowledge of textile production, finish, and care through in-depth study, industry exposure, and individual hands-on projects, connecting fabric to purpose, investigating treatments, designing fabric, and practicing weaving. Major topics include production steps, dying finishes, and differences between ready-to-wear, runway, and haute couture.

courses.title: Principles of Human Services
special_notes: CONFIRMED ACTIVE per NLPS Review Doc (7/26 update) - pathway is NOT being phased out. Includes a required job shadowing project (suggested 4-hour minimum for Ivy Tech requirements).
courses.description: Explores the history of human services, career opportunities, and the role of the human service worker, focusing on target populations and community agencies designed to meet various population needs. Includes a required job shadowing project (suggested four-hour minimum). Encourages cultural awareness and appreciation of diversity across major racial and ethnic groups in the United States.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Human Services
special_notes: CONFIRMED ACTIVE per NLPS Review Doc.
courses.description: Examines key elements of effective human services delivery, including personal values, helping relationships, the impact of diversity, theories of helping, communication, problem-solving processes, crisis situations, abuse, and professional ethics. Provides training for identifying crisis characteristics and basic crisis intervention skills, with students evaluating their own strengths and limitations.

courses.title: Community Health Worker
special_notes: IMPORTANT NAMING UPDATE: per NLPS Review Doc, the state renamed course 7278 from 'Community Health Worker' to 'Advanced Social and Community Services' beginning 2026-27. FCHS's guide still uses the old title - functionally the same course, but worth updating the site's display title to match the new state name, or at least noting the rename to avoid confusion.
State also added a new capstone course, 7279 Social and Community Services Capstone, not currently on FCHS's department guide - worth checking if FCHS intends to offer it.
courses.description: Explores care coordination, case management, coaching, cultural competencies, the Human Services Code of Ethics, professional development, and employment opportunities for community health workers and case managers. Examines background knowledge of intellectual and developmental disabilities and community social services, presenting practical information on service availability and community resources. Renamed 'Advanced Social and Community Services' by the state beginning 2026-27.

courses.title: Career Exploration Internship
courses.description: A paid or unpaid work experience in the public or private sector providing workplace learning in an area of student career interests, exposing students to broad aspects of an industry or career cluster. Students participate in regularly scheduled meetings or seminars connecting academic learning to work-related experiences.
